All work

Product design / UI & UX / Figma prototype

Lions MMA.

One club community.
Every side connected.

A family booking their next class. A coach taking the register. A manager keeping several clubs moving. One connected design, shaped around the different things each person needs to do.

Scope

Member app · Staff workspace · Public website

Design work

User journeys · Interfaces · Reusable components

Project stage

Design & prototype

01 / The product challenge

More than
a booking app.

The hard part is connecting the people around a class. A parent manages several children, reception needs to know who can train, a coach needs the right register, and head office needs a view across clubs.

The design gives each role a focused workspace while keeping memberships, bookings, attendance and progress part of the same journey.

16main member app screens
11staff and coach screens
12desktop website page states, with mobile companions

Design scope counted from the Figma file; overlays and the mobile menu are additional. Example names, figures and photography belong to the prototype.

02 / Members & families

Less admin.
More time on the mats.

The app follows the member’s routine: join, choose a class, check in, track progress and manage the account. A parent can move between children without starting again.

03 / Behind the scenes

The same club.
A different view.

Staff screens are organised around responsibility. Daily operations, the front desk, coaching and head-office reporting each have their own priorities.

04 / Connected workflows

The details
between screens.

Registration includes duplicate-member recognition, separate consent choices and unfinished-form reminders. Booking considers membership eligibility, capacity and waiting lists.

The wider staff design also covers sign-ups, recurring timetables, coach cover, payment exceptions, targeted messages and expiring staff qualifications. These are designed workflows; payment, messaging and access enforcement still require implementation.

Join

Family profiles, health details, consent and membership selection.

Train

Eligible classes, bookings, QR passes and attendance registers.

Keep connected

Progress, grading, updates, payments and staff follow-up.

05 / Before the first class

A public front door
to the whole experience.

The responsive website introduces classes and clubs, answers first-visit questions and leads into free-trial booking. Community pages extend the story to Punjab projects, volunteering and donations.

Scrollable homepage design. Open the image to inspect the full page. Photography is placeholder imagery in the Figma design.

06 / Design language

Warm for families.
Clear for staff.

The app pairs warm neutral surfaces with Lions orange for primary actions, rounded cards and plain-English labels. Denser desktop layouts keep operational information visible without giving every role the same screen.

A shared design system supports buttons, inputs, navigation, feedback and status patterns. The public website takes a quieter monochrome direction, giving imagery and the orange identity more room.

What this case study shows

A designed product system.

These are Figma screens and prototype journeys. Production development, integrations, data migration, accessibility testing and launch validation are separate delivery stages. No live usage or business results are claimed.
